items.title: Flight Attendant Seat Assembly (Single or Dual Position)
Required Flight Attendant Seats
items.rem:
One seat position or assembly (dual position) may be inoperative provided:
a) Affected seat or seat assembly is not occupied,
b) Flight attendant(s) displaced by inoperative seat(s) occupies either an adjacent flight attendant seat or passenger seat which is most accessible to inoperative seat(s) so as to most effectively perform assign duties,
c) Alternate procedures are established and used as published in crewmembers manuals,
d) Folding type seat stows automatically or is secured in retracted position, and
Passenger seat assigned to flight attendant is placarded "FOR FLIGHT ATTENDANT USE ONLY".
NOTE 1: An automatic folding seat that will not stow automatically is considered inoperative.
NOTE 2: A seat position with an inoperative or missing restraint system is considered inoperative.
NOTE 3: Individual operators, when operating with inoperative seats, will consider locations and combinations of seats to ensure that proximity to exits and distribution requirements of applicable CAR's are met.
NOTE 4: If one side of a dual seat assembly is inoperative and a flight attendant is displaced to adjacent seat, adjacent seat must operate normally.

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Baggage is not stowed under seat with inoperative restraining bar,
b) Associated seat is placarded "DO NOT STOW BAGGAGE UNDER THIS SEAT", and
Procedures are established to alert Cabin Crew of inoperative restraining bar.

items.title: Seat Belt/Air Bag Restraint System
items.rem: May be inoperative provided affected seat is blocked and placarded "DO NOT OCCUPY" .

items.title: "Fasten Seat Belts While Seated" Signs or Placards
items.rem: One or more signs or placards may be illegible or missing provided a legible sign or placard is visible from each occupied passenger seat.

items.title: Nonessential Equipment and Furnishing (NEF)
items.rem:
May be inoperative, damaged, or missing.
NOTE 1: Exterior lavatory door ashtrays are not considered NEF items.
NOTE 2: Infant seat belts in excess of those required for operations may be missing, provided Cabin Crew are notified for general awareness. Belts that are damaged or soiled shall be removed at the next practicable maintenance base for repair/replacement.

items.title: Non-Essential Electrical Equipment – Galley Oven / Water Boiler / Beverage Maker / Refrigerator / Lavatory Water Heater.
items.rem:
Equipment may be inoperative or missing, provided associated circuit breaker is pulled and collared. Only one item may be missing from the forward galley and one item from the rear galley.
NOTE: For water leakages refer MEL 38-01.

May be inoperative provided:
a) A passenger seat in passenger cabin is made available to a CASA Inspector for performance of official duties, and
b) Repairs are made within 2 flight-days.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Required minimum safety equipment (safety belt and oxygen) is available,
b) Seat is acceptable to a CASA Inspector for performance of official duties, and
c) Repairs are made within 2 flight-days.
NOTE 1: These provisos are intended to provide for occupancy of above seats by a CASA Inspector when minimum safety equipment (safety belt and oxygen) is functional and inspector determines conditions to be acceptable.
NOTE 2: Pilot-in-Command will determine if minimum safety equipment is functional for other persons authorized to occupy any observer seat(s).

items.title: Observer Seat Not Required by CAR's. (Including Associated Equipment)
items.rem: NOTE: Pilot-in-Command will determine if minimum safety equipment is functional for other persons authorized to occupy any observer seat(s).

items.title: Cabin
items.rem: May be inoperative or missing provided crewmember assigned to affected position has a flashlight of equivalent characteristics readily available.

items.title: Flight Deck
items.rem: May be inoperative or missing provided crewmember assigned to affected position has a flashlight of equivalent characteristics readily available.

items.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Lining Panels and Floor Panels
items.rem: May be damaged or missing provided procedures are established and used to ensure associated compartment remains empty or is verified to contain only empty cargo handling equipment, ballast and/or Fly Away Kits.

items.title: First Aid Kit (FAK) and/or Associated Equipment

items.rem:
If more than one is required by CAR's, only one required first aid kit may be incomplete, missing, or inoperative provided:
a) FAK is resealed in a manner that will identify it as a unit that cannot be mistaken for a fully serviceable unit, and
Repairs or replacements are made on first landing at a maintenance base.

items.title: Universal Precaution Kit
items.rem: Any in excess of the minimum required may be inoperative.

items.title: Airplanes with Multiple Exterior Lavatory Door Ashtrays Installed

items.rem:
Up to and including 50% maybe missing or inoperative for 10 days.
NOTE: Crew lavatories are included in the total aircraft exterior lavatory door ashtray count.

More than 50% may be missing or inoperative for 3 days.
NOTE: Crew lavatories are included in the total aircraft exterior lavatory door ashtray count.

items.title: Airplanes with Only One Exterior Lavatory Door Ashtray Installed
items.rem: May be missing provided it is replaced within 3 days.

items.title: Recline Mechanism
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Seat is secured in a position acceptable to affected crewmember, and
b) Repairs are made within 2 flight-days.

items.title: Vertical Adjustment
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Seat is secured in a position acceptable to affected crewmember, and
Repairs are made within 2 flight-days.

items.title: Armrests
items.rem: May be inoperative in up position or removed provided seat is acceptable to affected crewmember.

items.title: Lumbar/Thigh Supports
items.rem: May be inoperative provided seat is acceptable to affected crewmember.

items.title: Headrests
items.rem: May be inoperative or missing provided seat is acceptable to affected crewmember.

items.title: Galley Waste Receptacle Access Doors/Covers
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated container is empty,
b) Container access is secured to prevent waste introduction into compartment, and
c) Procedures are established to ensure that sufficient galley/lavatory waste receptacles are available to accommodate all waste that may be generated during flight.

items.title: Lavatory Waste Receptacle Access Doors/Covers
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated container is empty,
b) Container access is secured to prevent waste introduction into compartment,
c) Lavatory is used only by crewmembers, and
d) Associated lavatory entrance door is locked closed and placarded "INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER".
NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspection by crewmembers.

items.title: Storage Bins/Cabin, Galley, and Lavatory Storage Compartments/Closets

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Procedures are established to secure the affected bin, compartment, or closet in the closed position,
b) Affected bin, compartment, or closet is prominently placarded "DO NOT USE",
c) Any emergency equipment located in affected bin, compartment, or closet is considered inoperative, and
d) Affected bin, compartment, or closet is not used for storage of any item(s) except for those permanently affixed.
NOTE: For overhead bins, if no partitions are installed, the entire overhead bin is considered inoperative.

items.title: Galley Carts
items.rem: Any amount may be inoperative provided there is sufficient storage capacity for catering purposes.

May be inoperative provided:
a) For non-retractable doors, affected door is removed,
b) For retractable doors, affected door is removed or secured in the retracted (fully open) position,
c) Affected bin, compartment, or closet is not used for storage of any items except those permanently affixed,
d) Affected bin, compartment, or closet is prominently placarded "DO NOT USE",
e) Procedures are established and used to alert crewmembers and passengers of inoperative bins, compartments, or closets, and
f) Passengers are briefed that affected bin, compartment, or closet is not used.
NOTE 1: For overhead bins if no partitions are installed, entire overhead bin is considered inoperative.
NOTE 2: Any emergency equipment located in the affected bin, compartment or closet (permanently affixed) is available for use.

items.title: Multi Latch/ Quarter-Turn Lug Installations
items.rem:
One latch/lug per compartment may be inoperative provided:
a) Remaining latch(es)/lug(s) on affected compartments operates normally, and
b) If affected compartment is used for a galley cart, cart remains empty.

items.title: Storage Compartment Key Locks
items.rem: May be inoperative in the unlocked position provided doors can be secured by other means.

items.title: Cockpit Smoke Vision System (CSVS)
items.rem: May be inoperative or missing.

items.title: Security Kit and/or Associated Equipment
items.rem: May be inoperative, missing, or have missing equipment.

items.title: In-Flight Entertainment System (IFE). VH-RQC, VH-RQG, VH- RQP, VH-REX.
Wi-Fi IFE System/Components
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided the system is de-activated and Cabin Crew are notified that the entire Wi-Fi IFE system is inoperative.
Note: De-activation of the Wi-Fi IFE system will render GoGo connectivity system inoperative.

items.title: GoGo Connectivity System/Components
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided the system is de-activated and Cabin Crew are notified that the GoGo connectivity system is inoperative.
Note: De-activation of the GoGo connectivity system will render Wi-Fi IFE system inoperative.

items.title: Automatic Cargo Loading System - AFT
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided the system is de-activated in the most forward position.
Note: Any portion of the system that operates normally may be used.

items.title: Engine and APU Fire Extinguisher Discharge Lights
Engine Overheat and Fire Detection Systems
Dual Loop
items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one loop (A or B) per engine may be inoperative.

items.title: Portable Fire Extinguishers
items.rem:
Any in excess of those required by AD/GEN/65 may be inoperative or missing provided:
a) Inoperative fire extinguisher is tagged inoperative, removed from installed location, and placed out of sight so it cannot be mistaken for a functional unit, and
Required distribution is maintained.

May be inoperative provided procedure is used to ensure brakes are cool before engine start.
NOTE 1:Avoid the possibility of retracting an overheated wheel by leaving landing gear extended for 10 minutes after takeoff.
NOTE 2:In case of engine failure after V1, landing gear should be retracted until takeoff obstacles are cleared.

items.title: APU Fire Shutoff System
items.rem: Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided APU is not used.

items.title: APU Fire Extinguisher System
items.rem: Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided APU is not used.

items.title: Single and Dual Loop
items.rem: Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided APU is not used.

items.title: APU DET INOP Light
items.rem:
May be inoperative extinguished provided:
a) APU fire detection system operates normally, and
b) A fire warning test is performed before each APU start.

items.title: Dual Loop
items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one loop (A or B) may be inoperative.

items.title: External Warning Horn/Warning Light
items.rem: May be inoperative for ground operation provided flight deck APU Overheat/Fire Protection Panel is continuously monitored.

items.title: Engine/APU Fire Extinguisher Test System (EXT TEST) (Squib Test)
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Failure is verified to be in squib test circuit.
b) Squib circuit is verified to operate normally once each flight-day.

items.title: APU Fire Extinguisher Squib Test Circuits (EXT TEST)
items.rem: May be inoperative provided remaining APU Squib test circuit is verified to operate normally once each flight-day.

items.title: APU Squib Light
items.rem: Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided APU is not used.

items.title: Bell Cutout Switch (Overheat/Fire Protection Panel)
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Bell cutout function of both Master Fire Warning lights operates normally, and
b) Fire Warning Bell operates normally.

items.title: Bell Cutout Function of Master Fire Warning Light
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Bell cutout function switch operates normally, and
Fire Warning Bell operates normally.

Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided:
a) Right pack and engine bleed is used for pressurization only,
b) Use of APU is prohibited except for engine start,
c) Isolation valve and left engine bleed valve remain closed for all operations except engine start,
d) Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions, and
Flight altitude remains at or below FL 250.

Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided:
a) Left pack and left engine or APU bleed air is used for pressurization only,
b) Isolation valve and right engine bleed valve remain closed for all operations except engine start,
c) Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions, and
Flight altitude remains at or below FL 250.
For each lavatory, lavatory fire extinguisher system may be inoperative provided associated lavatory smoke detection system operates normally.

For each lavatory, lavatory fire extinguisher system may be inoperative provided:
a) Lavatory waste receptacle is empty,
b) Associated lavatory door is locked closed and placarded: "INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER", and
c) Lavatory is used only by crewmembers.
NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspection by crewmembers.

items.title: Passenger Configuration
items.rem:
For each lavatory, lavatory smoke detection system may be inoperative provided:
a) Lavatory waste receptacle is empty,
b) Associated lavatory door is locked closed and placarded: "INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER", and
c) Lavatory is used only by crewmembers.
NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspection by crewmembers.

items.title: Lavatory Smoke Detector SELF TEST Switch
items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated lavatory smoke detector is verified to operate normally.

items.title: Lavatory Smoke Detector TEST Switch on Flight Attendant's Panel
items.rem: May be inoperative provided each lavatory smoke detector is verified to operate normally.

items.title: Flight Deck Test Feature
items.rem: May be inoperative provided system integrity is verified by an acceptable procedure once each flight-day.

items.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Fire Detection/Suppression Systems
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided procedures are established and used to ensure associated compartment remains empty or is verified to contain only empty cargo handling equipment, ballast and/or Fly Away Kits.
NOTE : Class E cargo compartments require only installation of smoke or fire detection systems (not suppression).
One loop (A or B) in each compartment may be inoperative provided opposite loop is checked to operate normally.

items.title: No. 2
items.rem: Except for ER operations, may be inoperative with cargo carried in compartment.
May be inoperative provided associated extinguisher bottle(s) is verified to have an adequate charge once each flight-day.

items.title: Extinguisher Bottle Pressure Switch
items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated extinguisher bottle(s) is verified to have an adequate charge once each flight-day.

items.title: EXT Lights (FWD and AFT)
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Failure is verified to be in squib light circuit, and
Squib circuit is verified to operate normally once each flight-day.

items.title: DETECTOR FAULT Light
items.rem: May be inoperative provided the cargo fire TEST switch is used to check for faults in the cargo fire detection and suppression system before each flight.

items.title: Leading Edge Flap/Slat Position Light Systems

items.rem: Aft overhead LE DEVICES Annunciator panel may be inoperative provided forward panel lights operate normally.

Forward panel lights may be inoperative provided:
a) Aft overhead LE DEVICES Annunciator panel operates normally and is used to verify proper LED position, and
A placard is installed to indicate proper position for flap configuration in use.

items.title: Leading Edge Slat Indications
items.rem:
Indication lights on forward panel, and in addition, indication lights for one leading edge slat, except for slats 3, 4, 5, and 6, on overhead annunciator panel may be inoperative provided:
a) Normal operation is verified by flightcrew before each takeoff and landing,
b) Maximum speed is limited to 300 KIAS at/below FL 200 or .65 Mach above FL 200,
c) All remaining indications on overhead annunciator panel operate normally, and
Stall warning operation of both systems is verified to operate normally.

May be inoperative provided:
a) System is deactivated,
b) Operations are conducted in accordance with AFM, and
For models with Blended Winglet or Split Scimitar Winglet with Speed Brake Load Alleviation System, Speed Brake Load Alleviation System is considered inoperative.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Flaps are not extended beyond Flaps 30 at gross weights above 42,635 kg, and
Flaps are not extended beyond Flaps 15 at gross weights above 47,570 kg.

items.title: FEEL DIFF PRESS Light System
items.rem: May be inoperative provided Elevator feel system is verified to operate normally once each flight-day.

items.title: Auto Slat Fail Light System
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Auto slat systems are verified to operate normally, and
Verification is repeated every 2 flight-days.

items.title: Auto Slat Systems
items.rem:
One system may be inoperative provided:
a) Remaining auto slat system is checked to operate normally, and
Auto Slat fail light operates normally.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Control Surface Position Indication System is installed and operates normally,
b) Rudder trim actuator is checked to operate normally, and
c) Rudder trim is checked to be centered before each departure.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Rudder trim actuator is checked to operate normally, and
Rudder trim is checked centered before each departure.
May be inoperative provided speedbrakes are verified to operate normally.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Speedbrake handle forces are normal from full down to full up position,
b) Airspeed does not exceed 265 KIAS when in-flight gross weight is in excess of 70,306 kg,
c) Severe turbulent air penetration speed is 265 KIAS or 0.76 Mach, whichever is lower, when in-flight gross weight is in excess of 70,306 kg, and
d) Automatic Speedbrake System is considered inoperative.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Speedbrake handle forces are normal from full down to full up position, and
Takeoff weight does not exceed 70,533 kg.

items.title: STBY RUD ON light
items.rem:
May inoperative provided:
a) Rudder is verified to operate normally on hydraulic systems A and B independently,
b) Standby hydraulic pump is verified to operate normally, and
Rudder force fight monitor is deactivated.

items.title: Elevator Tab Control Springs
items.rem:
One may be broken or missing provided:
a) Broken spring is removed, and
Repairs are made within 10 flight-days.

items.title: Aft Pumps
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative provided:
a) Both main tank forward pumps operate normally,
b) At start of takeoff, fuel quantity in associated tank is not less than 3,402 kg,
c) A minimum fuel quantity of 1,134 kg is maintained in associated tank, and
d) Boost pump is deactivated.

items.title: Forward Pumps
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative provided:
a) Both main tank aft pumps operate normally,
b) At start of takeoff, fuel quantity in associated tank is not less than 2,177 kg,
c) A minimum fuel quantity of 817 kg is maintained in associated tank, and
Boost pump is deactivated.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Tank remains empty, and
b) Boost pump is deactivated.

May be inoperative with center tank fueled provided:
a) Fuel quantity remaining in main wing tanks is adequate to reach a suitable airport if remaining center pump fails at any time,
b) Zero fuel weight calculations are adjusted by weight of center tank fuel,
c) Effect on airplane balance, in event fuel cannot be used, is accounted for,
d) LOW PRESSURE light of operating center fuel tank pump operates normally,
e) Center tank quantity indication operates normally, and
Boost pump is deactivated.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Center tank quantity indication operates normally,
b) Center tank remains empty or zero fuel weight calculations are adjusted by weight of center tank fuel, and
c) Boost pump is deactivated.
NOTE: AFM Limitations for fuel loading must be observed.

items.title: Universal Fault Interrupter (UFI)
items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated center tank boost pump is considered inoperative.

items.title: Fuel Boost Pump Low Pressure Warning Light Systems
Main Tank Pump Low Pressure Warning Light Systems
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated fuel pump is not used, and
MASTER CAUTION lights and FUEL system annunciator light are verified to operate normally.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Both pumps in associated tank operate normally, and
b) Associated tank quantity indicator operates normally.
May be inoperative for an associated inoperative pump.

items.title: Center Tank Pump Low Pressure Warning Light Systems

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated fuel pump is not used, and
b) MASTER CAUTION lights and FUEL system annunciator light are verified to operate normally.

May be inoperative provided:
a) Center tank fuel is not required for flight,
b) Center tank fuel boost pumps are turned off, and
Center tank remains empty or zero fuel weight calculations are adjusted by weight of center tank fuel.

items.title: Center Tank Pump Lights
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Center Tank Fuel Quantity Indicator operates normally, and
MASTER CAUTION lights and FUEL system annunciator light are verified to operate normally.

items.title: APU Fuel Valve
items.rem:
Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided:
a) APU is not used, and
Valve is deactivated closed.

items.title: Crossfeed VALVE OPEN Light
items.rem:
Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided:
a) Crossfeed valve is verified to operate normally,
Fuel quantity indication for both main tanks operates normally.

items.title: Flight Deck Fuel Quantity Indicators (Main Tanks)
items.rem:
Except for ER operations, one may be inoperative provided:
a) All boost pumps in associated tank operate normally,
b) Fuel flow meters operate normally,
c) Center tank indicator operates normally,
d) Flightcrew periodically computes fuel remaining, or checks fuel remaining against a precomputed fuel burn chart, and
Fuel quantity in associated main tank is verified by an acceptable procedure.

items.title: Flight Deck Fuel Quantity Indicator (Centre Tank)

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) One center tank boost pump operates normally, and
Center tank remains empty.

Except for ER operations, may be inoperative provided:
a) Both center tank boost pumps operate normally, and
Fuel quantity in center tank is verified by an acceptable procedure.

items.title: Fuel Temperature Indicator
items.rem: May be inoperative provided Total Air Temperature or Ram Air Temperature is substituted as an indication of fuel temperature.

items.title: Pressure Fuelling System
items.rem: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are established and used.

items.title: Fuelling Manifold Check Valves
items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated Fueling Shutoff Valve is verified to operate normally.

items.title: Fuelling Shutoff Valve
items.rem:
May be inoperative closed provided:
a) Verify the refuel valve is closed by pressurizing the fueling manifold and verify that fuel does not flow to the tank with the failed refuel valve, and
b) After removal of the fueling nozzle, check the fueling receptacle for leakage. Leakage is not allowed.

items.title: Refuel Panel Fuelling Power Control Switch
items.rem: May be inoperative off provided refuel panel indicator test switch operates normally in AUX FUELING POWER CONTROL position or FUEL DOOR SWITCH BYPASS position as applicable.

items.title: Refuelling Control Panel Quantity Indicators
items.rem: May be inoperative provided fuel quantity is verified by an acceptable procedure.

items.title: Fuel Measuring Sticks/Dripsticks
items.rem: May be inoperative or broken/missing provided fuel quantity is determined by other acceptable means.
May be inoperative with fuel scavenge shutoff valve closed.
May be inoperative with fuel scavenge shutoff valve open provided No. 1 Main Fuel Tank forward boost pump remains off.
May be inoperative with fuel scavenge shutoff valve open provided center tank remains empty.

items.title: SPAR VALVE CLOSED Lights
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated valve is verified to operate normally, and
Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light operates normally.

items.title: Centre Tank Fuel Boost Pump Automatic Shutoff System

items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated centre tank fuel boost pump is considered inoperative.
May be inoperative provided centre tank remains empty.

May be inoperative with centre tank fueled provided:
a) Both centre tank fuel boost pump Low Pressure Warning Light Systems operate normally,
b) Centre tank fuel quantity indication operates normally,
c) Centre tank fuel boost pumps must not be ON unless personnel are available in the flight deck to monitor low pressure lights,
d) For ground operations, centre tank fuel boost pump switches must not be positioned to ON unless the center tank fuel quantity exceeds 453 kg, except when defueling or transferring fuel,
Center tank fuel boost pumps are OFF for takeoff if center tank fuel is less than 2,300 kg with airplane readied for initial taxi,
e) Both centre tank fuel boost pumps are selected OFF when centre tank fuel quantity reaches 453 kg of fuel during climb and cruise,
f) Both centre tank fuel boost pumps are selected OFF when centre tank fuel quantity reaches 1,400 kg of fuel during descent and landing,
g) Both centre tank fuel boost pumps are positioned OFF at first indication of fuel pump low pressure,
h) Centre tank fuel boost pumps may be positioned ON when established in cruise flight if the centre tank contains more than 453 kg of fuel,
i) If the main tanks are not full, the zero fuel gross weight of the airplane plus the weight of centre tank fuel may exceed the maximum zero fuel weight by up to 2,300 kg for takeoff, climb, and cruise and up to 1,400 kg for descent and landing provided that the effects of balance (CG) have been considered, and
Defueling with passengers on board is prohibited.

items.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve Battery and Charger
items.rem: May be inoperative deactivated.

items.title: Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump Depressurization Function

items.rem:
One may be inoperative provided:
a) System pressure is checked before each departure, and
b) All hydraulic low pressure lights operate normally.

items.title: System A Pump Low Pressure Indication Systems
items.rem: One may be inoperative provided output of associated pump is checked before each departure.

items.title: System B Pump Low Pressure Indication Systems
items.rem: One may be inoperative provided output of associated pump is checked before each departure.

items.title: System A and B Overheat Light System

items.rem: May be inoperative provided associated Low Pressure light operates normally.

items.title: Hydraulic Quantity Low Level Light System (Standby System)
items.rem: May be inoperative provided quantity is verified adequate before each departure.

items.title: Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump Depressurization Function
System A Quantity Indication System (Flight Deck)

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Quantity is verified adequate before each departure,
b) System pressure indication operates normally, and
Pump low pressure lights operate normally.

items.title: Standby System Low Pressure Light
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Standby system low quantity light operates normally,
b) Output of standby pump is verified before each departure, and
Both System B pumps operate normally.

items.title: Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization System Sources
items.rem: May be inoperative provided reservoir can be pressurized.

items.title: System B Quantity Indication System (Flight Deck)
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Quantity is verified adequate before each departure,
b) System pressure indication operates normally, and
Pump low pressure lights operate normally.

items.title: Hydraulic Reservoir Air Pressure Indicator (Wheel Well)
Wing Anti-Ice Valves
items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, may be inoperative closed provided airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.

One may be inoperative open provided:
a) Except for engine start, associated manifold is depressurized when outside air temperature is above 50 °F (10 °C),
b) Associated engine bleed thrust limits are followed when manifold is pressurized, and
Air conditioning and pressurization requirements are followed when one manifold is depressurized.

items.title: Wing Anti-Ice Valve Position Lights
items.rem: May be inoperative provided valve is verified to operate normally before operating in known or forecast icing conditions.

items.title: Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valves

items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative closed provided airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.

One may be inoperative locked open provided:
a) Associated High Stage Valve is considered inoperative,
b) Ambient temperature is below 100 °F (38 °C),
c) A minimum of 60% N1 is maintained on associated engine during flight in icing conditions, and
Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.

items.title: Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valve Position Lights or TAI Indications

items.rem: May be inoperative provided valve is verified to operate normally before each departure.
One valve position indication (either COWL VALVE OPEN light or TAI indication) for each engine may be inoperative provided other valve position indication for that engine operates normally.
May be inoperative provided associated valve is considered inoperative.

items.title: Left/Right Pitot Heaters
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative for day VMC provided:
a) Aux Pitot heater operates normally,
b) Airplane is not operated in visible moisture, and
c) Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.

items.title: Aux Pitot Heater (Right Lower Probe)
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, may be inoperative provided:
a) Both Left and Right Pitot heaters operate normally, and
Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.

items.title: Vertical Stabilizer Pitot Heaters (Elevator and Rudder Feel Systems)
items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative provided airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, may be inoperative provided airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
May be inoperative provided an alternate temperature indicator system is installed and operating normally (i.e., Ram Air or Static Air Temperature).

items.title: Angle of Attack Sensor Heater(s)/Stall Warning System Sensor Heater(s)/Alpha Vane Heater(s)
items.rem: Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, may be inoperative provided airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.

items.title: Pitot, Pitot/Static and Temperature Probe Heater Lights
Pitot and Pitot/Static
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, may be inoperative provided:
a) Associated heater function is verified to operate normally, and
Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
May be inoperative provided associated heater function is verified to operate normally before each departure.
May be inoperative provided associated heater is inoperative.

items.title: No. 1 Window
items.rem:
Except for ER operations beyond 120 minutes, one may be inoperative provided:
a) Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions,
b) Both No.2 window heaters operate normally,
c) Windshield defog system operates normally, and
d) Airspeed is limited to 250 KIAS below 10,000 ft. MSL.

items.title: No. 2 Window
items.rem:
One may be inoperative provided:
a) Both No. 1 window heaters operate normally,
b) Windshield defog system operates normally, and
c) Airspeed is limited to 250 KIAS below 10,000 ft. MSL.

items.title: No. 4 or No. 5 Window
items.rem: No. 4 and No. 5 window heat may be inoperative provided airspeed is limited to 250 KIAS below 10,000 ft. MSL.

items.title: Windshield Defog System
items.rem: May be inoperative provided electrically heated windshields for No. 1 and No. 2 windows operate normally.

items.title: Windshield Wiper System(s)
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:

items.title: FDR Recording Parameters Required by CAO 103.19.

For EFIS/MAP configuration, one may be inoperative provided:
a) It is checked that engine display can be switched to an alternate DU,
b) All navigation must be based on ILS/VOR/DME, and
Repairs are made within 1 flight-day.

a) Operation of associated systems is not affected, and
All takeoffs and landings are made by pilot with access to an operating tiller.

items.rem: May be inoperative provided brake accumulator charge is verified normal once each flight-day.

items.title: Gear Retraction Braking System

May be inoperative provided:

items.title: Landing Gear Selector Valve Bypass Module
items.rem: May be inoperative provided it is deactivated in normal position.

items.title: Landing Gear Actuation System
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:

b) Landing gear is secured in down position, and
Airplane is dispatched in accordance with AFM Gear Extended Appendix.
NOTE: Dispatch under this MEL requires GMFO/CP or B737 Fleet Manager approval.

items.title: Proximity Switch Electronics Unit (PSEU) System and Supplemental Proximity Sensor Electronics Unit (SPSEU)

items.rem: May be dispatched with faults indicated by PSEU light provided PSEU is checked for faults before each departure.
May be dispatched with faults indicated by PSEU light provided PSEU light can be extinguished.

items.rem: May be inoperative provided PSEU is checked for faults before each departure.

items.title: Landing Gear Alternate Extension System
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Inoperative Components are secured by an accepted procedure,
b) Landing gear is secured in down position, and
Airplane is dispatched in accordance with AFM Gear Extended Appendix.
NOTE: Dispatch under this MEL requires GMFO/CP or B737 Fleet Manager approval.

items.title: Main Landing Gear Uplock Springs
items.rem: One spring on one main gear uplock mechanism may be missing provided landing gear lever remains in UP position for duration of flight until gear extension is required.

items.title: Landing Gear Frangible Fitting
items.rem: May be broken or missing provided fitting is replaced with a hydraulic cap assembly.

items.title: Flap Landing Warning Switch, S138
items.rem:
Switch contacts normally in use may be inoperative provided:
a) S138 switch is rewired using an alternate set of contacts, and
b) PSEU BITE is used to verify normal operation of S138 switch.

items.title: Cockpit/Flight Deck/Flight Compartment and Instrument Lighting System
items.rem:
Individual lights may be inoperative provided:
a) Remaining Lighting System lights are sufficient to clearly illuminate all required instruments, controls, and other devices for which they are provided,
b) Remaining Lighting System lights are positioned so that direct rays are shielded from flightcrew members' eyes, and
c) Lighting configuration and intensity is acceptable to the flightcrew.
NOTE 1: Individual button/switch lights and/or annunciation/indications are excluded from this relief.

items.title: Cabin Illumination with Photoluminescent Emerg Escape Path Lighting
items.rem:
Individual lights may be inoperative provided:
a) Sufficient lighting remains for cabin attendants to perform their duties, and
b) Remaining lighting is sufficient to charge the photoluminescent escape path system

items.title: Passenger Lighted Information Signs and Notice System
"NO SMOKING/ FASTEN SEAT BELT/ RETURN TO SEAT" Signs

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:
a) Associated passenger seat or lavatory is not occupied from which a passenger lighted information sign is not readily legible, and
b) Associated seat or lavatory is blocked and placarded "DO NOT OCCUPY".
NOTE: These conditions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspections by crewmembers.

a) PA system operates normally, and PA system is used to notify passengers and cabin crew when associated sign(s) are placed on or off.

items.title: Aural Tone System
items.rem: Flight crew must agree alternate communication procedures with the flight attendants including flight crew making PAs in place of the aural tone.

items.title: Flight Deck Automatic Function
items.rem:
May be inoperative provided:

Alternate procedures are established and used.

b) Operations are not conducted at night or in conditions of poor visibility.

items.title: Wing Tip Position Lights
items.rem: May be inoperative provided operations are not conducted from sunset to sunrise or in conditions of poor visibility.

items.rem: Light assemblies installed above aisle may be inoperative provided no two adjacent (opposite side) light assemblies are inoperative.

items.title: Flight Deck Exit Light
items.rem: May be inoperative provided operations are not conducted at night.

May be inoperative for an associated inoperative system.

items.rem: May be inoperative provided intended function of associated light(s) is verified once each flight-day.

items.title: Floor Proximity Emergency Escape Path Marking System
Incandescent Lighting System
items.rem:
Individual lights may be inoperative, provided:
A. All floor aisle marker lights which indicate exit locations must be operative.
B. The most forward and farthest aft floor aisle marker lights must be operative.
C. Every other floor aisle marker light must be operative (no two adjacent marker lights may be inoperative).
D. Sidewall exit indicators must have two of the five lamps operating.

items.title: Photoluminescent Lighting System
items.rem:
Components may be inoperative provided:
A. Sidewall exit indicators must have three of the five lamps operating.
B. A maximum of 5 inches of any length of standard photoluminescent strip between 15 inches and 72 inches in length may be inoperative.
C. A maximum of 5 inches of any length of colored photoluminescent strip between 15 inches and 79 inches in length may be inoperative.

items.title: Seat Mounted LED and Incandescent Lighting Systems
items.rem:
Individual lights may be inoperative provided:
A. All monument mounted lights are operative.
B. All lights within two seat rows of a monument (including a class divider) must be operative.
C. All lights within two seat rows of the Type III Exit must be operative.
D. No two adjacent seat mounted lights may be inoperative.
E. All flood lights and exit identifiers must have two of the five lamps operating.

items.title: Master Dim System
items.rem:
Dim function may be inoperative provided:
a) TEST and BRT functions operate normally,
b) Except during light test, switch is placed in BRT, and
Light intensity is acceptable to flightcrew.

items.rem: May be inoperative provided operations are not conducted at night.

Airspeed remains at or below 320 KIAS.

a) Both Mach indicators operate normally,
b) 330 KIAS/.76 Mach airspeed limitations are observed, and If overspeed warning occurs below .76 Mach, system must be deactivated by pulling associated circuit breaker and observe speed limits.

a) Operations are conducted in Day VMC only, and
Operations are not conducted into known or forecast over-the-top conditions.

a) Any combination of two gyro or INS (IRU) stabilized compass systems are operative, and
b) Airplane is operated with dual independent navigation capability and under positive radar control by ATC on enroute portion of flight.

items.rem: May be inoperative provided approach minimums do not require its use.

items.title: Weather Radar with Windshear Detection and Avoidance System (Predictive) Installed

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided the aircraft does not depart if the relevant forecasts or reports indicate that potentially hazardous weather conditions exist:
(a) in the flight path along which the aeroplane will be flown; or
(b) if the operational flight plan for the flight includes an alternate aerodrome— in the flight path to the alternate aerodrome.
NOTE: Reactive Windshear Warning and Guidance System must be operative for dispatch.
potentially hazardous weather conditions means such potential weather conditions as can be detected by airborne weather radar equipment.
relevant forecasts or reports means any of the following:
(a) an authorised weather forecast in relation to the flight;
(b) an authorised weather report in relation to the flight.

items.title: Weather Radar without Windshear Detection and Avoidance System (Predictive) Installed

items.rem:
May be inoperative provided the aircraft does not depart if the relevant forecasts or reports indicate that potentially hazardous weather conditions exist:
(a) in the flight path along which the aeroplane will be flown; or
(b) if the operational flight plan for the flight includes an alternate aerodrome— in the flight path to the alternate aerodrome.
potentially hazardous weather conditions means such potential weather conditions as can be detected by airborne weather radar equipment. relevant forecasts or reports means any of the following:
(a) an authorised weather forecast in relation to the flight;
(b) an authorised weather report in relation to the flight.

NOTE: Qty 1 must be operative for ILS approach.

items.title: Elementary and Enhanced Downlink Aircraft Reportable Parameters Not Required by CAR's.
items.rem:

a) Autopilot with altitude hold and altitude capture operates normally,
b) Enroute operations (i.e., RVSM) do not require its use,
c) Airplane does not depart from an airport where repair or replacement can be made, and
d) The flight begins within 72 hours of the time the equipment was found to be inoperative;
NOTE: TCAS must be operative.

b) Autopilot with altitude hold and altitude capture operates normally.

a) Aural alert operates normally, and
b) Autopilot with altitude hold and altitude capture operates normally.

items.rem:

NOTE: The aeroplane must not depart from an aerodrome where facilities are available to repair or replace the GPWS. An aerodrome is deemed to have "facilities" if there are appropriately approved staff, equipment (tooling) and parts available to repair or replace the unserviceable items.

items.title: Modes 1 thru 4

NOTE: The aeroplane must not depart from an aerodrome where facilities are available to repair or replace the GPWS. An aerodrome is deemed to have "facilities" if there are appropriately approved staff, equipment (tooling) and parts available to repair or replace the unserviceable items.

NOTE : If a Cargo Fire Panel FWD/AFT warning light does not illuminate during system test, one or more detection loops for the associated cargo compartment is inoperative.
To determine the inoperative loop(s):
1. On the Cargo Fire Panel, position the FWD and AFT DET SELECT switch to A.
2. Press and hold Cargo Fire Panel TEST switch.
3. Verify that the following indications occur within 4 seconds.
A. Fire Bell sounds.
B. Both Master FIRE WARN lights illuminate.
C. Cargo Fire Panel FWD and AFT warning lights illuminate.
D. Cargo Fire Panel DISCH light illuminates.
E. Cargo Fire Panel EXT FWD and EXT AFT lights illuminate.
4. If one or more smoke detectors in Loop A is inoperative, the Cargo Fire Panel DETECTOR FAULT light will illuminate and the associated FWD or AFT warning light will remain extinguished for the cargo compartment with the inoperative detector.

6. Position Cargo Fire Panel FWD and AFT DET SELECT switch to B and repeat the above test (Steps 2 through 5).
7. Position Cargo Fire Panel DET SELECT switch(es) as required for flight. One detection loop (A or B) must operate normally in each cargo compartment or OMEL loading restrictions must be observed.

2. Verify that the LE DEVICES annunciator panel (P5) operates normally during flap extension and retraction. NOTE: If an annunciator panel TRANSIT light fails to illuminate while the corresponding device is in motion, then this light must be considered inoperative.

With forward position indicator lights inoperative and one SLATS annunciator panel light inoperative:
1. Verify leading edge slat position for the inoperative indication before each takeoff and landing.
2. Limit airspeed:
A. At or below FL 200, limit airspeed to 300 KIAS.

1. Cycle the flaps.
2. Verify that the remaining LE DEVICES annunciator panel (P5) lights operate normally during flap extension and retraction.
NOTE 1: If an annunciator panel TRANSIT light fails to illuminate while the corresponding device is in motion, then this light must be considered inoperative.
NOTE 2: This OMEL item is applicable to inoperative leading edge SLAT indications and not the leading edge FLAP indications on the LE DEVICES annunciator panel. Dispatch is not allowed if the LE DEVICES annunciator panel FLAP lights do not illuminate properly and the forward panel light(s) are inoperative.
3. Remove the bulbs from the associated forward position indicator light(s) on the center instrument panel, P2.
4. Use this data to make a placard and put it adjacent to the annunciator panel:
A. Flap positions 1 thru 5:
1) All slats in EXT position.
2) LE flaps extended.
B. Flap positions 10 thru 40:
1) All slats in FULL EXT position.
2) LE flaps extended.
5. Determine which TE flap position(s) result in inoperative indication.
A. If faulty indication is intermittent or cannot be replicated on the ground, use FSEU BITE to determine if an FSEU input has been recently faulty:
1) If FSEU BITE (Flight Leg 0) indicates fault message codes 27-81200 through 27-81223 or 27-81225 through 27-81236, open and collar the Stall Warning Asymmetry Mode circuit breaker on the P18-2 Panel.
B. If FSEU BITE does not yield one of these fault codes because the fault indication light(s) flashes ON/OFF for an instant such that the fault does not latch, and the applicable slat can be confirmed to be stationary in the position where the intermittent indication was observed, then open and collar the Stall Warning Asymmetry Mode circuit breaker.
NOTE: The FSEU will inhibit the Takeoff Warning (TOW) alert to the PSEU when 7 of 8 LE slats are extended during a takeoff attempt ONLY if circuit breaker C1208 Stall Warning Asymmetry Mode is open. If the circuit breaker is closed, the TOW will occur when the crew advances the throttles for takeoff.
6. Set flaps to the position which produces the faulty indication.
7. Verify that the leading edge and trailing edge devices are in the correct position.
8. Verify normal operation of both Stall Warning Systems:
NOTE 1: If the inoperative slat indication occurs at more than one flap position, repeat the procedure to verify normal operation of both Stall Warning Systems at Flaps 0, Flaps 1 and Flaps 10.

1. Prior to takeoff, make sure that the speed brake lever is in the full down detent.
2. Perform an OPT computation with the selected MEL item.
NOTE: OPT will base Landing performance on Manual speed brakes.
3. Extend speedbrakes manually for rejected takeoff or landing.
A. For rejected takeoff:
1) Simultaneously close the thrust levers, disengage the autothrottles and apply maximum manual wheel brakes or verify operation of RTO autobrakes.
2) Manually raise SPEED BRAKE lever.
3) Apply the maximum amount of reverse thrust consistent with conditions.
B. For landing:
1) Simultaneously close the thrust levers and apply manual wheel brake or verify operation of autobrakes.
2) Manually raise SPEED BRAKE lever.
3) Apply reverse thrust consistent with conditions

27-10:
Verify that the feel system is operative once each flight day (AMM 27-00-00/901):
1. Pressurize the elevator hydraulic systems A and B (AMM 27-31-00/201).
CAUTION: MAKE SURE PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE HORIZONTAL TAIL AND ARE AWARE THAT HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS ARE PRESSURIZED.
2. Use the stabilizer trim switches to set the stabilizer to 4 units of trim.
3. Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches to OFF.
4. Verify that the horizontal stabilizer "B" dimension is 39.89 ± 0.01 inches.
5. Set the mach trim actuator in null position (AMM 27-31-00/201).
6. Do a check for pressure leakage in the feel pitot system:
A. Apply a seal to the drain hole in each feel pitot tube on the vertical fin.
B. Remove the drain plugs from the system A and B pitot lines.
NOTE: The pitot lines are located below the elevator feel computer.
C. Connect the pressure gage lines from the air pressure regulator to the drain holes of the pitot lines. CAUTION: DO NOT RAISE TEST PRESSURE ABOVE 5.0 PSI (437 KNOTS) AT ANY TIME DURING TEST.
D. Connect the pressure lines from air pressure regulator to both pitot probes on the vertical fin.
E. Pressurize the pitot system to 4.8 ± 0.1 psi (429 ± 4 knots).
F. Turn the shutoff valve in the air pressure regulator to off.
G. Make sure the pressure does not decrease more than 0.3 psi (12 knots) during a 2-minute period.
H. Reduce the pitot pressure to zero.
7. Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches to ON.
8. Pressurize the pitot system to 2.47 ± 0.05 psi (315 ± 3 knots). CAUTION: DO NOT RAISE TEST PRESSURE ABOVE 5.0 PSI (437 KNOTS) AT ANY TIME DURING TEST.
9. Apply masking tape on the tail cone along the direction of the right elevator trailing edge travel.
NOTE: Elevator travel measuring tool may be used in lieu of tape method.
10. Move the captain's control column lightly to put the elevator system in the neutral position.
NOTE: Make sure that the control columns are not disturbed from this position during the next step.
11. Mark the actual elevator trailing edge neutral position on the masking tape.
12. Set FLT CONTROL B switch to OFF and leave FLT CONTROL A switch in the ON position.
13. Move the captain's control column slowly with a push/pull type spring scale applied to the center of the control wheel to the elevator positions as shown in the table below. NOTE: Make sure the force to hold the control column is as below:
14. Elevator Position - 1.20 ± 0.05 inches up - Column Force – 17.24 ± 1.8 kgs
15. Elevator Position - 1.20 ± 0.05 inches down – 17.24 ± 1.8 kgs
16. Set FLT CONTROL A switch to OFF and FLT CONTROL B switch to ON.
17. Do step 13 again.
18. Restore the airplane to its usual condition:
A. Make sure that all tools used during testing are removed.
B. Remove all masking tape.
C. Remove seals from the drain holes in each vertical fin pitot probe.
D. Remove the pressure gage lines from systems A and B drain lines.
E. Install the drain plugs to the systems A and B drain lines.
F. Remove regulated air pressure lines from both vertical fin pitot probes.
G. Close all circuit breakers opened during testing.
H. Restore airplane to normal hydraulic configuration (AMM 27-31-00/201).
I. Remove electrical power if no longer required.

27-14-01:
Confirm normal operation of the rudder trim actuator and confirm rudder trim is centered before each departure.
1. Pressurize rudder hydraulic systems A and B.
2. Do a test of the rudder trim actuator:
A. Turn the rudder trim knob to the NOSE LEFT position.
B. Observe that the captain's left rudder pedal moves forward and right rudder pedal moves aft.
C. Turn the rudder trim knob to the NOSE RIGHT position.
D. Observe that captain's left rudder pedal moves aft and right rudder pedal moves forward.
3. Do a test of the rudder trim centering:
A. Turn the rudder trim knob in appropriate direction until the captain's rudder pedals are aligned with each other.
B. Make sure that the rudder is centered (in the neutral position). If not, use rudder trim until rudder is centered.
27-14-02:
Confirm normal operation of the rudder trim actuator and confirm rudder trim is centered before departure:
1. Pressurize rudder hydraulic systems A and B.
2. Do a test of the rudder trim actuator:
A. Turn the rudder trim knob to the NOSE LEFT position.
B. Observe that the captain's left rudder pedal moves forward and right rudder pedal moves aft.
C. Turn the rudder trim knob to the NOSE RIGHT position.
D. Observe that captain's left rudder pedal moves aft and right rudder pedal moves forward.
3. Do a test of the rudder trim centering:
A. Turn the rudder trim knob in appropriate direction until the captain's rudder pedals are aligned with each other.
B. Make sure that the rudder is centered (in the neutral position). If not, use rudder trim until rudder is centered.
27-16-02:
Verify normal operation of the speed brakes (AMM 27-00-00/901).
1. Verify that wheel chocks are in place.
2. Put the SPEED BRAKE lever in the DOWN position.
3. Visually verify that flight and ground spoilers are all down.
4. Put the SPEED BRAKE lever in the FLIGHT DETENT.
5. Visually verify that ground spoilers and flight spoilers deploy.
6. Put the SPEED BRAKE lever in the DOWN position.
7. Visually verify that flight and ground spoilers are all down.
8. Verify that stabilizer trim is in the green band.
9. Position flaps to a takeoff position.
10. Release the parking brake.
11. Advance (engines not running) both thrust levers beyond 60 degrees.
12. Make sure that the Takeoff Configuration Warning Horn does not sound.
13. Retard thrust levers to idle.
14. Return airplane to it's normal configuration, i.e., set parking brake and retract flaps.
15. If the SPEEDBRAKES EXTENDED light remains illuminated while on the ground, extinguish it by removing the light bulb.

1. Verify that the rudder operates normal on hydraulic system A and B:
A. Pressurize hydraulic systems A and B.
B. Set FLT CONTROL A switch ON and FLT CONTROL B switch OFF.
C. Verify normal rudder pedal forces by pushing captain's left rudder pedal forward (while holding tiller to prevent tire scrub) until it touches the stop and hold.

I. Set FLT CONTROL B switch ON and FLT CONTROL A switch OFF.

Verify the cause of malfunction and inspect oil filter for contamination (AMM 79-00- 00/901).
1. Remove the scavenge oil filter element (AMM 79-21-06/401).
2. Visually inspect the scavenge oil filter element. If the filter element is not contaminated, the malfunction is in the bypass warning system.
3. Visually inspect the scavenge oil filter element for contaminants once each flight day.
79-02-02:
For dispatch, perform the following verification steps once each flight day:
1. Verify the malfunction is in the bypass warning system:
A. Verify presence of fault code 79-n112x on the FMC CDU (AMM 73-21- 00/501).
B. If fault code 79-n112x is not present, access the CDU INPUT MONITORING / OIL FILTER screen on the FMC CDU and verify FILTER BYPASS state is "CLOGGED", which corresponds to the following FILTER INPUTS displayed on the FMC CDU: Switch 1 (Channels A and B) OPEN, Switch 2 (Channels A and B) CLOSED.
2. Inspect all three Magnetic Chip Detectors for contaminants (AMM 79-00-00/601).
3. Verify the oil supply filter pop-out indicator is not extended. (AMM 79-00-00/601).
4. If Magnetic Chip Detectors inspection reveals no contaminants and oil supply filter pop-out indicator is not extended, then the malfunction is in the warning system.

Check that the associated start valve is closed after engine start.
1. Use normal start procedures except for the following:
A. Prior to selecting ENGINE START switch to GRD position note the duct pressure.
B. For airplanes without automatic ignition, as ENGINE START switch moves to OFF, verify that duct pressure returns to the pre-start value or higher.
C. For airplanes with automatic ignition, as ENGINE START switch moves to AUTO, verify that duct pressure returns to the pre-start value or higher.
2. If duct pressure does not return to the prestart value or higher, dispatch is not allowed. In this case, shutdown the affected engine as follows:
A. Position the ISOLATION VALVE switch to CLOSE.
B. Position the affected engine BLEED air switch to OFF.
C. If the affected engine is the left engine and APU bleed air is being used, position the APU BLEED air switch to OFF.
D. Remove ground air source, if being used.
E. Set the affected engine start lever in the CUTOFF position.

1. Perform normal start procedure with following additions:
A. When positioning associated ENGINE START switch to GRD position, instruct ground crew to open start valve.
B. Inform ground crew when N2 is rotating.
C. Instruct ground crew to close the start valve when indication is 56% N2 RPM.
D. Without automatic ignition: Verify that the ENGINE START switch moves to OFF
E. With automatic ignition: Verify that the ENGINE START switch moves to AUTO.
